source.title: Latent Programming Horizons in Coding Agents
source.authors: André Silva; Han Tu; Martin Monperrus

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether hidden states anticipate future program outcomes using linear probes and a step-based lookahead horizon. This is a conceptual test of future-state decodability, not a test of future-token prediction or causal steering.
record.gate_note: The future-edit horizon results bear on the claim. Current-program probes, layer-selection values, and cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: New setting: coding agents on SWE-Bench. Linear probes on hidden states predict program properties k agent steps ahead. This bears on V5 (look-ahead beyond verse) much as chess and Sokoban future-move probing does. No causal intervention is made, and nothing is measured on future tokens or rhyme.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude hidden states encode current program properties and predict future edit outcomes above chance up to ~25 steps, with a weak plateau to k=50. They frame this as a coding analogue of look-ahead and explicitly say it does not show causal use.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear probes to predict program-property labels at future agent steps, rather than measuring future-token prediction or intervening on a candidate future token. No causal intervention is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: Lookahead horizon, transformer layer, benchmark, model, and program property are varied. The text reports that prediction decays with horizon and differs between benchmarks; performance is strongest in intermediate layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Current-program properties (parse, pass tests, fewer failing tests, regressions) are linearly decodable at k=0. AUC reaches 0.83 (Qwen full correctness), peaks in middle layers, and transfers across benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coding-agent residual streams encode current program semantic state (world-model style, not planning).

record.problems: Probe decodability does not demonstrate causal use. Only two open-weight models, one agent scaffold, and two benchmarks are studied. The main text gives approximate horizon values without uncertainty estimates; several further results are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Current-program-property probing results were left out because they do not measure future lookahead. Figure-only lookahead curves for other model/property combinations were not extracted as separate rows because the text does not provide assignable numeric values for them.

untested.parts: All: no rhyme or verse, no frontier model.
All: predicts program-property labels at future agent steps, not tokens at future positions.
All: no test of whether features are computed for later use.
Causal use of look-ahead (authors state decodability is not causality). Chess, Sokoban and multi-step reasoning are not studied.
Whether the future-outcome signal reduces to current-state or local features is not tested. No control for current label or task difficulty.

missing.what: k=0 reference AUC on the lookahead test set (full correctness ~0.77 Verified, ~0.82 Pro), needed to see the size of the decay
Lookahead curves for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and for the partial-correctness, well-formedness and regression probes (figure-only)
k≤15 lookahead replication without the length filter (figure-only)

record.verdict_notes: The main validity concern is not noted in the record: labels are carried forward until the next edit, and most trajectories have few edits. Future-step labels therefore often equal current labels, and final correctness is partly a task-level property. Above-chance future AUC may reflect state persistence or task difficulty rather than planning. The shuffled-label control is reported only for current-state probes. Steps are agent turns, not tokens.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representation and interventions that change verse lines.
Predicting tokens several token positions ahead; the study predicts properties of future program versions at future agent steps.
Whether features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction; no causal intervention tests this.
Rhyme planning in open-weight models or open attribution-graph/probing tools.
The study tests lookahead in coding-agent tasks, not multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban.
The study measures future program-property decodability, not whether those representations causally steer edits or are incidental next-token features.

rows.subject: Laguna-XS.2
rows.operation_detail: Linear probe on a hidden state predicts full correctness of the program at a future agent step.
rows.measure: AUC for predicting future program full correctness
rows.note: The text reports the value around k=25 as part of the declining lookahead curve; it does not specify a layer for this summary.
rows.check: V6 link removed: the study does not test whether the signal comes from local features or heuristics. Value ~0.55 at k≈25 is only slightly above 0.50. Labels persist until the next edit (median 2 edits per trajectory), and no control for the current label is reported. Some future-label AUC may therefore be current-state carryover or task difficulty, not look-ahead. Layer is unspecified; the 0.50 is the nominal random line, not a shuffled-label probe at k>0.

relationships.condition: Laguna-XS.2, SWE-Bench-Verified and SWE-Bench-Pro, full-correctness probe at k≈25 and k=50
relationships.reason: Future correctness is only weakly decodable (~0.52–0.65 AUC, r1–r4) and decays steeply from k=0. Persistent labels are not controlled and no steering is done, so look-ahead is not separated from current-state readout.
relationships.display_finding: Future-correctness probes achieved approximately 0.52–0.65 AUC at k≈25 and k=50, declining steeply from k=0; uncontrolled label persistence and absent steering left current-state explanations unresolved.
